author: WP12
summary: Alpha.1-era chapter on content hardening: where limits are enforced, trust rules for names versus internal references, recursion bounds, fuzzing, differential oracles, error normalisation and remaining asymmetries. Several asymmetries are closed at TARGET (SpriteFont list lengths, exact Texture3D/TextureCube levels, glTF validation, wrapped glTF errors through Load<Model>) while new ones appear on reading (untyped object path without a depth guard, late LZX length check). The site held individual limits on several pages; a cross-format hostile-input deep dive now carries the whole picture.

sections.heading: Limits are useful only where they are enforced
Top-level names and internal references have different trust rules
Object graphs are bounded on both recursive axes

concepts.text: Content loading combines attacker-controlled lengths, recursion, compression, paths, decoders and GPU allocations; the honest account states enforcement points and remaining gaps without a blanket safety or insecurity claim.
tokens: without turning either into a blanket claim of safety

concepts.text: The XNB side went through a substantial hardening campaign while CNJ and glTF keep narrower controls.
tokens: Limits are useful only where they are enforced

concepts.section: Limits are useful only where they are enforced
concepts.text: XNB decoded payload is bounded at 256 MiB on the size hint and the final decoded length.
tokens: Declared size at most 256 MiB before decoding

concepts.section: Limits are useful only where they are enforced
concepts.text: Reader-table names are bounded at 1 MiB after ReadString, reader counts at 4,096, object and type nesting at 256 and shared resources at 1,000,000 before fixups.

concepts.section: Limits are useful only where they are enforced
concepts.text: maxFileSize (64 MiB) protects a compressed payload only after the whole XNB has been read into memory; an oversized uncompressed file allocates before any guard; the build-time importer is where 64 MiB is a real admission check.
tokens: The first row is the canonical warning against reading a constant's name as a guarantee

concepts.section: Limits are useful only where they are enforced
concepts.text: CNJ has no document-size and no JSON depth limit: the whole text is read and the parser recurses freely.

concepts.section: Limits are useful only where they are enforced
concepts.text: CNB bounds file size (512 MiB, before reading), chunk and total logical sizes, strings, counts and alignment, and checks CRC-32C on every structure, which the XNB and CNJ routes lack.
tokens: At most 512 MiB, checked before reading
CRC-32C over header, table of contents and each chunk's stored bytes

concepts.section: Limits are useful only where they are enforced
concepts.text: LZX output is compared with the declared size only after the last block, while LZ4 is bounded at every step; CNB Zstandard chunks are checked before allocation and must expand exactly.
tokens: The two XNB decompressors differ in when they stop

concepts.section: Top-level names and internal references have different trust rules
concepts.text: ContentManager::Load<T> deliberately accepts an explicit absolute name and RootDirectory is a base, not a sandbox; containment applies to paths supplied inside content.

concepts.section: Top-level names and internal references have different trust rules
concepts.text: Logical XNB external references reject absolute spellings and normalisation above the root before re-entering the manager; filesystem-shaped CNJ sourceFile, sidecar and embedded media paths add weakly canonical symlink checks against their authorised root.
tokens: Paths written inside content are contained

concepts.section: Top-level names and internal references have different trust rules
concepts.text: Containment compares component by component after optional weakly_canonical, never by string prefix, so content-evil is not a child of content.

concepts.section: Top-level names and internal references have different trust rules
concepts.text: A referring file inside the content root is confined to the root, while one loaded through an explicit outside-root path is confined to its own folder, keeping external bundles loadable.

concepts.section: Top-level names and internal references have different trust rules
concepts.text: Containment tests cover traversal, absolute and drive paths, Unicode-shaped input and existing-symlink escapes, assert rejection before file access without cache poisoning, and keep . segments, repeated separators and inside-root .. legal.

concepts.section: Top-level names and internal references have different trust rules
concepts.text: Symlink checking is not race-proof: weak canonicalisation followed by a later open leaves a time-of-check to time-of-use window, so escapes are refused in the checked filesystem state only.
tokens: Symlink checking is not claimed to be race-proof

concepts.section: Object graphs are bounded on both recursive axes
concepts.text: XNB has two recursion surfaces, canonical reader names and nested object dispatch; both are capped at 256 on the typed path.
tokens: Recursion: two axes bounded, two open

concepts.section: Object graphs are bounded on both recursive axes
concepts.text: The object path uses an RAII guard that decrements on success and on every exception so one failed read cannot poison the session's remaining depth.
tokens: cannot use up the session's remaining depth

concepts.section: Object graphs are bounded on both recursive axes
concepts.text: Claim that object graphs are bounded on both recursive axes without qualification: at the snapshot the untyped object path (InnerReadObjectAny) is not depth-counted, and CNJ JSON and reference cycles through the manager are also unbounded.
tokens: no load is marked as in progress
concepts.note: Untyped gap and cycles established by reading.

concepts.section: Object graphs are bounded on both recursive axes
concepts.text: Shared resources use a two-pass discipline: counts and indices are validated before fixups are queued and every shared object is read before any fixup runs, preserving identity across forward references.
The strongest container fuzz target mutates complete real XNB fixtures by flipping, truncating, overwriting and inserting bytes and loads them through the real ContentManager::Load<T>.
Acceptable fuzz outcomes are success or an enumerated clean exception; std::bad_alloc is recorded as an allocation-guard failure, not a valid rejection.
A second target mutates LZX payloads and the decompressed-size hint, requiring every successful decode to produce exactly the declared length.
The fuzz targets found memory-safety defects review did not: the Texture2D device-dimension check was added after real crashes (Vulkan stack smashing, a non-catchable WebGPU panic).
tokens: These targets found defects that review did not

concepts.text: Fuzz coverage now also includes the CNB container codecs and the XNB writers' inputs; the build offers CNA_SANITIZE for sanitizer runs.
CNJ has no equivalent document fuzzer.
tokens: there is no CNJ document fuzzer

concepts.text: Claim that glTF production code does not call cgltf_validate: at the snapshot ValidateGltfEXT calls cgltf_validate, checks alignment and enforces required extensions before import.
concepts.note: Bible (alpha.1-era) said no validation; TARGET validates.

concepts.text: The LZX decoder is compared byte for byte with FNA's unmodified C# decoder under Mono, because a compressor and decoder sharing one mistaken assumption can agree with each other.
tokens: A writer and a reader that share one wrong assumption agree with each other

concepts.text: Texture and audio readers use other independent checks: level byte counts against block-rounded format expectations, the stored duration as a broad audio oracle, and real fixtures from several producers.
tokens: every texture level's byte count against the block-rounded size

concepts.text: Each oracle has a stated scope: duration agreement cannot prove waveform identity and a storage round trip cannot prove shader sampling.
tokens: Each oracle has a stated scope

concepts.text: Container and reader errors are generally translated to ContentLoadException with asset context, and the name parser's std::invalid_argument is caught at the reader-table boundary.
tokens: a caller needs one exception type for a malformed table

concepts.text: Claim that some glTF extraction failures escape as plain std::runtime_error: through Load<Model> they are now wrapped by the loose tier into ContentLoadException; only direct calls into the glTF import core see std::runtime_error.
concepts.note: Wrapped at TARGET for the Load<Model> route.

concepts.text: Custom CNJ factories can throw arbitrary exceptions, which the loose tier wraps; the SoundEffect loose tier and XNB/CNB object constructors stay unwrapped, so callers cannot assume one dynamic exception type.

The container fuzzer's accepted exception list is the precise statement of what a malformed .xnb can raise through Load<T>: ContentLoadException, EndOfStreamException, the ArgumentException family, profile-refusal NotSupportedException, bad_any_cast, out_of_range, length_error and invalid_argument.
Asymmetry still present: the initial whole-XNB read is uncapped by maxFileSize.
Asymmetry still present: CNJ has neither size nor depth controls and mixes the strict parser with substring scanners in the Model, custom-GLSL Effect and skinned-model readers.
tokens: still reads Model, custom-GLSL Effect and skinned-model fields with substring scanners

concepts.text: Claim that SpriteFont does not cross-check its parallel glyph, crop, character and kerning table lengths: at the snapshot it does.
tokens: SpriteFont refuses glyph, cropping, character and kerning lists of different lengths

concepts.text: Claim that Texture3D and TextureCube mip topology and compressed-byte exactness are weaker than Texture2D's: at the snapshot per-level bytes are exact under a cumulative budget for both; what remains weaker is that dimension limits are left to texture creation.
tokens: Texture3D and TextureCube readers leave dimension limits to texture creation

concepts.text: Symlink containment is not TOCTOU-proof.
tokens: Symlink containment is not time-of-check to time-of-use proof

concepts.text: A low-severity misaligned read in the vendored cgltf sparse-accessor path remains listed as an accepted residual in CNA's own integration records (REMED-CONTENT-010).
concepts.note: Attributed to CNA's records; not re-verified in third_party. Post-Phase-3 adversarial audit correction: the C08 review found this ledger correction wrong: the accepted residual was superseded by GLTF-036 (audit finding C08 ch37-content-robustness-F1).

concepts.text: The remediation record is credible because the gaps are named: one critical and several high-severity content findings were closed, and extending the same observable limits and fuzz discipline to the asymmetric formats is the remaining work.
tokens: is the remaining work the asymmetries describe

issues.text: glTF import errors escaping catch(ContentLoadException&): through Load<Model> the loose tier now wraps them; direct GltfImportCore callers still see std::runtime_error.
glTF input never validated against its declared requirements: ValidateGltfEXT now runs cgltf_validate, an alignment check and extensionsRequired enforcement.
Vendored cgltf misaligned sparse-accessor read listed by CNA as a LOW accepted residual (REMED-CONTENT-010).
